listeningQuestions.audio: Disappointed by his behaviour, I told my best friend everything.
opts: 对他的行为感到失望,我把一切都告诉了好友。

listeningQuestions.audio: I was only letting off steam when I complained about my teammate.
opts: 我抱怨队友时只是在发泄情绪。

listeningQuestions.audio: A sincere apology can repair a damaged friendship.
opts: 真诚的道歉能修复受损的友谊。

listeningQuestions.audio: Good friendships, like the porcupines, need a little space.
opts: 好的友谊就像豪猪一样,需要一点空间。

listeningQuestions.audio: Take a deep breath and calm down before you speak in anger.
opts: 生气说话前,先深吸一口气冷静下来。
他把秘密告诉了所有人。

listeningQuestions.audio: Honesty is the core of every true friendship.
opts: 诚实是每段真挚友谊的核心。

quizQuestions.q: Speaking too freely can cause all kinds of ____ between friends.
Trust is the ____ value of any close friendship.
A true friend gives you ____ comments so that you can improve.
First, you should ____ to your teammate for your careless words.
____ by his behaviour, I told my best friend everything.
____ more time, most people will do a better job.
____ about her sick friend, Anna could not focus on her homework.
____ in this way, your friendship will soon be repaired.

opts: 他被当众批评,感到很尴尬。
我们一个接一个地自我介绍。
quizQuestions.audio: Criticised in front of others, he felt very embarrassed.

opts: 被好友的支持打动,她内心感到温暖。
quizQuestions.audio: Touched by her friend's support, she felt warm inside.

reading.passage: True friendship is like the porcupines on a cold night: we need each other for warmth, yet we also need a little space. Stand too close, and small differences begin to hurt; stay too far, and we feel cold and alone. The wisest friends find a comfortable distance built on honesty and trust.
reading.passageCn: 真正的友谊就像寒夜里的豪猪:我们既需要彼此取暖,也需要一点空间。靠得太近,小小的分歧便会伤人;离得太远,又会感到寒冷孤单。最明智的朋友会找到一个建立在诚实与信任之上的舒适距离。

questions.q: According to the passage, what happens if friends stand too close?
What do the wisest friends find?
opts: A comfortable distance built on trust.

writing.prompt: Write 3-4 sentences about how you would deal with a small conflict with a friend. Say what happened, what you did, and how you felt. Try to use one -ed participle as an adverbial (e.g. Hurt by his words, I …).
writing.promptCn: 用3-4句话写写你会怎样处理和朋友的一次小冲突:发生了什么、你怎么做、你的感受。试着用一个 -ed 分词作状语(如 Hurt by his words, I …)。

lines.text: I need to talk to you. You told everyone what I said about the match.
lines.cn: 我得跟你谈谈。你把我说的关于比赛的话告诉了所有人。

lines.text: I'm really sorry. I didn't think before I spoke, and I let you down.
lines.cn: 我真的很抱歉。我没多想就说出口了,辜负了你。

lines.text: I was only letting off steam. I never wanted the whole team to hear it.
lines.cn: 我只是在发泄情绪,根本不想让全队都听到。

lines.text: You're right. From now on, I'll keep your words to myself, I promise.
lines.cn: 你说得对。从现在起,我保证守口如瓶。
